Join two tables

Source: R/join.R
join.Rd

join() matches the rows of x and y on key columns. Pairs come in x's row order and, within a row of x, in y's; right and full joins add y's rows in y's order. Key columns appear once, under x's names; for a row only y has, they take y's values.

Usage

join(x, y, on, how = "inner", multiple = "all", na_equal = TRUE, suffix = NULL)

Arguments

x, y

Zutables.

on

The keys: a column, .(a, b), or .(id == customer_id) where the names differ. Each pair of keys must have the same type.

how

"inner", "left", "right", "full", "semi" (the rows of x with a match) or "anti" (those without).

multiple

When a row of x matches several rows of y (for a right join, a row of y several of x): "all" pairs, the "first" or "last" match, or "error", a zutable_multiple_error.

na_equal

Whether a missing key matches a missing key: TRUE, as R and data.table do, or FALSE, as SQL does.

suffix

Two suffixes for non-key columns both tables have, such as c(".x", ".y"); without it such a clash is a zutable_schema_error.

Value

A zutable.

Examples

orders <- zutable(id = c(1L, 2L, 3L), customer = c(10L, 20L, 10L))
people <- zutable(customer_id = c(10L, 20L), name = c("Ada", "Linus"))
join(orders, people, on = .(customer == customer_id))
#> <zutable> 3 rows x 3 columns
#>   id      customer name
#>   <int32> <int32>  <string>
#> 1 1       10       Ada
#> 2 2       20       Linus
#> 3 3       10       Ada
join(orders, people, on = .(customer == customer_id), how = "anti")
#> <zutable> 0 rows x 2 columns
#>  id      customer
#>  <int32> <int32>
